messages:
Maya: Quick FYI — marketing's launching the new Pro Essentials bundle tomorrow 09:00 PT. They expect ~30% lift in Starter->Pro conversions during the first 72h. We need a fast headroom plan for GPU-backed endpoints.
Sam: Do we have a projection for token/hour or just seat conversions?
Maya: Early estimate from growth: ~40k extra generation requests/hr at median 200 tokens each (burst to 120k/hr peak). Rough calc = ~8M extra tokens/hr baseline, 24M peak.
Jonas: Ok rough mapping to GPU hours: with our m40-like profiles that's ~0.28 GPU-hours per 1M tokens (approx). So baseline +2.2 GPU-hours, peak +6.7 GPU-hours across region.
Elena: Which regions are we targeting? Marketing will run EU morning + NA afternoon, APAC only later week. So primary surge in eu-west and us-west.
Phil: Our EU pool is already at 82% reserved for Dedicated customers. We have ~6 spare GPUs but not all have the right kernel/quant combo for the new model configs.
Maya: We need a short plan: 1) immediate soft quotas on Starter->Pro ramp for first 48h, 2) reserve 8 GPUs (or equivalent vGPU share) in us-west + eu-west for 72h, 3) enable predictive autoscale with burst to preemptive queued tickets. Thoughts?
Sam: Soft quotas sound sensible. We should also enforce per-token rate limits per account to avoid single-customer storms. Add automatic rollback if 5xx rate >1% for any model route.
Jonas: Reserve ask: 8 GPUs for 72h ~ 576 GPU-hours. Cost estimate (spot-weighted): $3.6k if we use spot/pooled. If we require Dedicated SLA (for isolation) cost is closer to $9k.
Elena: Could we instead rebalance existing workloads via priority classes and preempt some low-priority batch jobs? That would reduce hard reservation cost.
Phil: Yes we can throttle low-priority job queues and shift background evals to off-peak. But that requires ops playbook and tagging which is half-ready.
Maya: For immediate action — Sam, can you create a soft-quota PR for Starter->Pro with an emergency bump path? Jonas/Phil please model the 576 GPU-hour reserve cost vs preemption plan by EOD so finance can approve.
Sam: On it. I'll add a 75% ramp cap for new Starter->Pro conversions and a 10min token leak-bucket per account. PR link will be in a few mins.
Jonas: I'll run quick sim with current kernels and quant settings. If we can switch some routes to int8 we drop CPU/GPU time ~22%, may avoid full reservation. Sending numbers in 45m.
Phil: I'll prepare capacity-bot rules: auto-burst to spare pool up to 4 GPUs, then fallback to soft-quota. Also add per-region alarm to page if latency > 200ms for 5m.
capacity-bot: [system] Scheduled job "predictive-capacity-scan" started for thread 1934567890. Scanning: 3 regions, 2 models, 72h window.
Elena: Also tagging note — any Dedicated customer impacted by throttling needs CS escalation path. I'll draft the customer communications template with explicit SLOs.
Maya: Thanks. If we get signoff from finance on the reserve cost, we should flip the marketing launch to night window to smooth EU->NA ramp. Can someone coordinate with growth?
Sam: I'll ping @growth in #marketing-live and propose the shift.
Jonas: Simulation update: switching to int8 for route A reduces token GPU time from 0.28 -> 0.21 GPU-hours per 1M tokens. Baseline reserve drops from 2.2 -> 1.65 GPUs equivalence. More detailed numbers in thread later.
Phil: Cost compare attached in the PR (short table) — preempt + throttle wins for cost, reserve wins for predictability. Decision needed by 07:30 PT.
Maya: Final ask: flag any infra changes that need deploy windows. We should avoid risky kernel swaps during the promo. Keep changes to config, quotas, and autoscale.
Sam: Understood. Quota PR will be config-only.
Jonas: Will run integration test against canary cluster, no kernel switch in prod until post-launch.
Maya: Great. Thanks all — keep updates in this thread and drop the PR links here.
capacity-bot: [system] Completed predictive-capacity-scan. Recommendation: prioritize preemption + 4 GPU burst across us-west/eu-west, enable int8 routes for route A, soft-quota 75% ramp. Confidence: medium.
